{{Quote|Six meters of muscle, teeth, and venom. Hyperfast reflexes and a vicious streak as wide as the Cron Drift. I'd say you're looking at the most efficient predator in history.|Tyro Viveca|<ref name="FP" />}}
'''Lamproids''', also known as '''Florn Lamproids''', were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Diet/Legends|carnivores]] from the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Florn/Legends|Florn]]. The countless dangers of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] had shaped them into consummate predators: they had well-muscled, [[Snake/Legends|serpentine]] coils that could constrict with deadly force, and mouths that could deliver mortal blows from rings of keen [[Tooth/Legends|fangs]]. They employed a venomous stinger at the tip of the tail and a milky venom in their saliva. The Lamproid body was segmented and had six short [[Limb/Legends|limbs]] with clawed pincers. A tiny, wet sensory filament curled from between their fangs to detect scent, and [[Eye/Legends|light stalks]] on their heads sensed a range of the spectrum beyond that of most species. Some possessed the ability to communicate feelings [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathically]], although this was not believed to be a species-wide trait.

Lamproids descended from intestinal [[Parasite/Legends|parasites]] that had evolved into independent, intelligent predators. They were primitive by most species' standards, lacking in both art and culture. However, their [[Brain/Legends|brains]] were excellent at solving puzzles. This made them popular prey for unscrupulous [[Hunting/Legends|hunters]] seeking a challenging hunt.

Members of the species spread beyond their homeworld and proved to be aggressive colonizers. They particularly thrived on jungle and forest planets, although they were known even on desert worlds like [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Although few [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] citizens knew much about the species and even mistook them for non-sentient pests, some Lamproids adapted to galactic technology and [[Galactic community|society]] and plied the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|starlanes]] as [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]], [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]], and [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]]. One such Lamproid was [[Dice Ibegon/Legends|Dice Ibegon]], agent of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and lover of [[Lak Sivrak/Legends|Lak Sivrak]].

==Biology and appearance==
===Dimensions and traits===
{{Quote|You have to get out of there. I will open this door.|Cecil Noone falls prey to Lamproid telepathy|<ref name="FP" />}}
[[File:Dice_ibegon.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Lamproids had snakelike bodies and fearsomely fanged mouths.]]
Lamproids were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]],<ref name="CSWE II 243" /> [[Worm/Legends|vermiform]]<ref name="FF CAN3">{{FactFile|22|CAN 1-6|Mos Eisley Cantina Characters}}</ref> invertebrates<ref name="OLN" /> related to intestinal [[Parasite/Legends|parasites]]. Their bodies were thick,<ref name="NEGAS" /> segmented<ref name="TLC" /> tubes of muscle<ref name="NEGAS" /> that grew to as long as six [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length<ref name="FP" /> and often twisted [[Snake/Legends|serpent]]-like into coils.<ref name="CSWE II 243" /> Their anatomy was roughly divided into three equal sections: head, thorax, and tail.<ref name="TLC" /><ref name="OLN" /> Six thin, jointed [[Limb/Legends|limbs]], each with a pair of sharp, claw-like pincers, extended from the midsection. Thin flaps of skin fringed the tapered tail,<ref name="TLC" /> a part of the body that doubled as a fine manipulator.<ref name="OLN" /> Veiny, wrinkled skin covered their bodies and came in shades of brown,<ref name="TLC" /> gray,<ref name="NEGAS" /> gray-green,<ref name="FP" /> and pink,<ref name="SWR" /> sometimes blotched with yellow<ref name="TLC" /> or sporting ring-like spots.<ref name="EI1/2">[[Episode I: The Phantom Menace ½|''Episode I: The Phantom Menace'' ½]]</ref> Lamproids crawled about on their bellies.<ref name="TLC" /> They could hold around 1.3 meters of their thorax and head upright;<ref name="NEGAS" /><ref name="TLC" /> one Lamproid of such height weighed forty-five [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]].<ref name="HTHTT">''[[Star Wars: Head-to-Head Tag Teams]]''</ref>

The Lamproid head was dominated by a slack, pulsating<ref name="CSWE II 243" /> oral cavity<ref name="SWC">''[[Star Wars Chronicles]]''</ref> lined with circles of [[Tooth/Legends|fangs]]<ref name="CSWE II 243" /> and surrounded by four longer mouthparts.<ref name="OLN" /> Their teeth could be many colors, including black<ref name="SWC" /> reddish-orange,<ref name="CSWE II 243" /> yellow, and white. A straw-like tongue<ref name="FP" /> unfurled from the central orifice to facilitate smell and taste,<ref name="NEGAS" /> and ingestion.<ref name="OLN" /> Four [[Eye/Legends|photosensitive stalks]] adorned the head<ref name="TLC" /><ref name="CSWE II 243" /> and allowed Lamproids to sense beyond most species' visual spectrum. By shifting these finger-like eye knobs, a Lamproid could monitor more than one direction at a time,<ref name="OLN" /> a handy adaptation to surviving in dangerous environments.<ref name="NEGAS" /> The eyestalks could be black<ref name="SWC" /> or pink;<ref name="SWR" /> they lost rigidity upon a Lamproid's [[Death/Legends|death]].<ref name="OLN" />

===Behavior===
[[File:Florn_Lamproid_front_view.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Dice Ilbegon, a Lamproid]]
The species was [[Diet/Legends|carnivorous]] and drank [[Blood/Legends|blood]].<ref name="CVD" /> Although non-Lamproids often found their appearance hideous and horrifying,<ref name="FP" /><ref name="FF CAN3" /> these fearsome adaptations had molded them into consummate predators.<ref name="FP" /><ref name="DI CCG">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Dice Ibegon}}</ref> Their rows of razor-sharp teeth<ref name="FP" /> were capable of shredding flesh,<ref name="OLN" /> and their milky, toxic saliva was able to fell large prey.<ref name="NEGAS" /><ref name="FP" /> The tail terminated in a barbed stinger that could deliver its own venom;<ref name="NEGAS" /><ref name="DI CCG" /><ref name="FL CCG">{{CCG|set=Jabba's Palace Limited|cardname=Florn Lamproid}}</ref> the optimal attack range for a Lamproid 1.3 meters in height was twelve meters.<ref name="HTHTT" /> The beings were known for their immaculate reflexes,<ref name="FP" /> incredible bursts of speed,<ref name="NEGAS" /><ref name="FP" /> and ferocious strength capable of separating a [[Bantha/Legends|bantha]] from its [[Bone/Legends|skull]]<ref name="OLN" />&mdash;features that served them equally well in offense and defense.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Members of the species emitted [[Pheromone/Legends|pheromones]] that signaled others and provided information such as whether a Lamproid was [[Gender/Legends|male or female]].<ref name="OLN" /> Some exhibited [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathic]] abilities as well. For example, when the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Con artist/Legends|conman]] [[Cecil Noone]] encountered a [[Unidentified Lamproid (Kabal)|caged female Lamproid]]<ref name="FP" /> in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> she slowly conveyed to him the notion to free her. The suggestion began as an itch at the back of his neck followed by a tickle inside his head. The sensation spread to his forehead and grew more pronounced and insistent. Finally, he experienced stress behind his eyes and then felt the strong urge to free the caged Lamproid. They could also dissipate mild pain. In the same encounter, Noone, who had an injured hand, felt the pain relieved. Nevertheless, the pain gradually returned after the Lamproid went free.<ref name="FP" />

Lamproids were endothermic,<ref name="NEGAS" /> and their blood was purple.<ref name="OLN" /> Individuals typically went about unclothed,<ref name="ANH" /><ref name="FL CCG" /> although those that had adapted to [[Galactic community|galactic society]] sometimes sported minimal trappings, such as a kerchief about the neck<ref name="ANH:M">[[Star Wars Manga: A New Hope 2|''Star Wars Manga: A New Hope'' 2]]</ref> or an insulated jumpsuit in arctic conditions.<ref name="OLN" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Aren't Florn lamproids sentient?''"<br />"''Unquestionably. Though they lack the culture and art you and I take for granted, they have the brains to solve fiendishly complex puzzles. That's what makes them such a smashing hunt.|Cecil Noone and Tyro Viveca, on Viveca's stuffed Lamproid specimen|<ref name="FP" />}}
Lamproids had no obvious culture and created no art,<ref name="FP" /> so many beings considered them little more than simple animals. Nevertheless, they were clever beings<ref name="NEGAS" /> and could solve complicated puzzles that required high levels of intelligence.<ref name="FP" />

Lamproids were aggressive,<ref name="CSWE II 243" /> natural-born [[Hunting/Legends|hunters]],<ref name="SWE">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> reputed to be among the most dangerous predators in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]<ref name="NEGAS" />&mdash;their instincts were so honed for the hunt<ref name="FP" /> that the smell of blood alone was enough to make a Lamproid's tail shake.<ref name="OLN" /> They hunted by first stalking their prey. Once a Lamproid felt confident enough to make a kill, he or she made a quicksilver strike at full strength and betrayed his or her presence with only a fearsome hiss. Once the prey was grappled, the Lamproid coiled its body around the prey and constricted his or her body to crush and suffocate the victim. Lamproids also attacked with their tail stinger, the venom of which was enough to put down a [[Houk/Legends|Houk]]. The mouthful of razor teeth was another potent weapon. Those Lamproids capable of telepathy could also attempt to get into the prey's head to cause pain and disorientation. When threatened, the tail stinger was the favored means of defense.<ref name="FP" />

Lamproids formed mating pairs.<ref name="FP" /> They felt genuine affection for one another and conveyed their compassion by intertwining their bodies. One Lamproid, the female [[Dice Ibegon/Legends|Dice Ibegon]], even entered a love affair with a member of a totally unrelated species, a [[Shistavanen/Legends|Shistavanen]] male named [[Lak Sivrak/Legends|Lak Sivrak]].<ref name="EGtC">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> Lamproids could learn to speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] with their hissing voices. Like other species, Lamproids communicated emotions via facial expressions, although their different morphology meant that they could not perform conventional actions like smiling. Instead, a Lamproid conveyed amusement by shifting its teeth.<ref name="OLN" /> Some Lamproids showed [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitivity]] and learned to communicate with others using [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="NEGAS" />

==History==
[[File:Lamproid-JabbasPalaceLimited.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Lamproids spread throughout the galaxy. One member of the species was part of Jabba the Hutt's court.]]
The Lamproids evolved on [[Florn/Legends|Florn]], a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] notorious for its perils. In fact, the planet was so dangerous that offworlders stood little chance of survival there for any significant length of [[Time/Legends|time]] without [[hyperaccelerated nerve implant]]s.<ref name="CSWE I 282">{{CSWECite|I|282|Florn}}</ref> Lamproids developed from intestinal parasites that eventually evolved the ability to live outside their hosts.<ref name="NEGAS" /> The species became the only species from their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] to develop sentience.<ref name="OLN" />

Outsiders from another planet arrived on Florn sometime between [[27,500 BBY|27,500]] and [[25,127 BBY]]. These explorers were [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]], and by [[25,096 BBY]], Florn&mdash;known at the time as "Tinatorn"&mdash;had been claimed as part of the expanding [[Xim's empire|empire]] of [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot]], considered a part of a region of the empire known as the [[Far Indrexu]].<ref name="EA" /> Despite Xim's death and the dissolution of his empire, Lamproids spread beyond the planet<ref name="NEGAS" /> and colonized many worlds.<ref name="FL CCG" /> In fact, [[Xenobiology|xenobiologists]] once believed that the species had no single homeworld and were instead native to several.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Members of the species particularly preferred worlds with large tracts of forest or jungle.<ref name="CSWE II 243" />

Between [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000]] and [[8000 BBY]], explorers from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] reached Florn for the first time.<ref name="EA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Although the world was for a time reckoned as part of [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]],<ref name="NEGAS" /> it eventually became part of the [[Pakuuni sector/Legends|Pakuuni sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Florn system/Legends|Florn system]]</ref> Several centuries prior to [[4166 BBY]], the [[Overic Griplink/Legends|Overic Griplink]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] connected Florn to the planets [[Dac/Legends|Mon Calamari]] to the east and [[Quermia/Legends|Quermia]] to the west, placing the Lamproids in contact with the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] and [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]] species native to the former. These connections also brought the Lamproid homeworld into various galactic conflicts such as when in [[3963 BBY]], the [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders]] won a [[Battle of the Florn system|battle]] there against the forces of the Galactic Republic during the [[Mandalorian Wars]] and when the world fell within territory controlled by [[Revan/Legends|Darth Revan]] during the [[Jedi Civil War]] of [[3959 BBY|3959]] to [[3956 BBY]]. The world was considered Galactic Republic territory from [[1004 BBY|1004]] to [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], a span of time during the [[New Sith Wars]], and of [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Realspace/Legends|Space]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="EA" />

Members of the species largely supported the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], and several Lamproids secretly worked as recruiters for the Rebellion.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Despite the Lamproids' Rebel sympathies, Florn became part of [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] [[Zsinj]]'s [[Zsinj's Empire|holdings]] in [[7 ABY/Legends|7]] and [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] splintered the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] into various Imperial splinter factions. By approximately [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], the population of the [[Florn system/Legends|Florn system]] had reached some 500 million to 1 billion inhabitants. In [[137 ABY]], it fell within territory controlled by [[Darth Krayt]] as part of his [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="EA" />

==Lamproids in the galaxy==
{{Quote|We are alike, as you have always known. The hunter and the killer know the sick and diseased must be culled from the herd&mdash;and the Empire is rotten with corruption. That is why you must leave me, to continue our fight until the end.|Dice Ibegon, to Lak Sivrak|<ref name="OLN" />}}
Although they had joined the galactic community as early as the reign of Xim the Despot<ref name="EA" /> and spread to many worlds,<ref name="FL CCG" /> to most citizens of the galaxy, Lamproids remained little-known<ref name="SWVD">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> and were often mistaken for non-sentient creatures.<ref name="NEGAS" /> In 0 ABY, this enabled the [[Krish (species)/Legends|Krish]] big-game hunter [[Tyro Viveca/Legends|Tyro Viveca]] to capture a mated pair and cage them on his estate on the planet [[Kabal/Legends|Kabal]]&mdash;despite the fact that Viveca himself knew the Lamproids to be sentient. The hunter killed the [[Unidentified Lamproid (Tyro Viveca's trophy)|male Lamproid]] and had the being's stuffed body on display in his home. He kept the female in a [[force cage]] to be hunted another day, but the conman Cecil Noone freed her after a con gone bad put him on the run from the Krish. The female Lamproid stalked her one-time tormentor and nearly killed him, but Viveca managed to decapitate her with his [[Hunting blaster/Legends|hunting blaster]], sacrificing another trophy to save his own life.<ref name="FP" />

[[File:BlackHoleCantina-SWR33.jpg|thumb|right|300px|In cantinas, such as Black Hole on Kiffex, Lamproids preferred blood-based cocktails.]]
Some Lamproids became acclimated to galactic-standard technology and society and made their way as [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] or [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]].<ref name="SWG">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=terminal||Lamproid Smugglers: a Messy Bunch}}</ref> For example, a Lamproid was present in a [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]<ref name="EI1/2" /> in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="TCC">''[[Star Wars: The Comics Companion]]''</ref> and another was at the [[Mos Espa Grand Arena/Legends|Mos Espa Grand Arena]] on that world during the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] that same year.<ref name="TPM:Game">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]</ref> Another was a patron of the [[Black Hole (Kiffex)|Black Hole]] cantina on the planet [[Kiffex/Legends|Kiffex]]<ref name="SWR" /> in [[30 BBY/Legends|30 BBY]].<ref name="SWR date">[[Star Wars (1998) 33|''Star Wars'' (1998) 33]] takes place thiry [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior to the events of {{Film|IV}}, which corresponds to [[30 BBY/Legends|30 BBY]] according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="swg date">{{SWG_timeline}}</ref> the [[Animal Control Division]] of the [[Corellian Security Force]] (CorSec) put out a briefing to [[mission terminal]]s on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] that alleged that the organization had caught a group of [[Unidentified Lamproid smugglers|Lamproid smugglers]] trying to stage a live game of [[Dejarik/Legends|dejarik]] using real creatures. The Lamproids split at the first sign of trouble and freed the beasts. CorSec offered a small reward to anyone willing to exterminate the smuggled animals.<ref name="SWG" /> Another Lamproid was part of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt's]] entourage and at one point traveled aboard Jabba's [[Sail barge/Legends|sail barge]], the [[Khetanna/Legends|''Khetanna'']].<ref name="FL CCG" /> Bartenders who were familiar with the species offered blood-based cocktails for such customers.<ref name="CVD" /> Clarified bantha blood was one of these beverages,<ref name="OLN" /> although other mixes had decidedly murkier origins.<ref name="CVD" />

Dice Ibegon was among the Lamproids to support the Rebel Alliance during the Galactic Civil War. In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], she visited the [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Mos Eisley Cantina]] on Tatooine to look for likely candidates<ref name="OLN" />&mdash;and came under brief inspection by the [[Gotal/Legends|Gotal]] [[Feltipern Trevagg/Legends|Feltipern Trevagg]], who was looking to hire an [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] to kill co-worker [[Predne Balu]]; he discounted the Lamproid when the vibrations she caused in his head [[cones]] disquieted him.<ref name="N:TLT">{{StoryCite|story=Nightlily: The Lovers' Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref> Ibegon met the Shistavanen Lak Sivrak at the cantina and convinced him to join the Alliance. The two became lovers and fought together in the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], but Ibegon died during the Rebel evacuation.<ref name="EGtC" /> Nevertheless, Ibegon had learned [[Force power/Legends|Force abilities]] such as telepathy and time shifting,<ref name="OLN" /> and she was able to guide Sivrak from the afterlife as a [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghost]]<ref name="CSWE II 74">{{CSWECite|II|74|Ibegon, Dice}}</ref> so that the two might be together forever in the afterlife.<ref name="OLN" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Notable appearances===
{{Quote|And [George] Lucas walked up and looked at it, too. He said, 'That's really a gross-looking thing! What kind of a rating do we have on this, Gary [Kurtz]?' 'Well, I think it's a PG.' So they said, 'Yeah, let's go ahead and shoot it!'|Phil Tippett recalls George Lucas and Gary Kurtz's initial reactions to the "drooling arm" cantina puppet|<ref name="TMOSW">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Florn_Lamproid_puppet_side_view.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The Dice Ibegon character from ''A New Hope'' was a puppet sculpted from the neck up.]]
The Lamproid species was designed for the cantina sequence of the [[original trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], released in [[1977]]. The character was a hand puppet created by [[Rick Baker]]'s special effects team along with the other [[Alien/Legends|alien]] characters who appear in close-ups shot during the film's post-production in [[Wikipedia:Los Angeles|Los Angeles]], [[Wikipedia:California|California]].<ref name="SWOPM 12">[[Star Wars Official Poster Monthly 12|''Star Wars Official Poster Monthly'' 12]]</ref> [[Phil Tippett]] designed the puppet to counterbalance the other cantina denizens, who were primarily human beings with masks. Tippett originally intended for the creature to simulate breathing through its mouth parts. The character was known as the "drooling arm" during production due to its ability to emit red slime through an internal tube.<ref name="TMOSW" />

In preparation for shooting the close-up featuring the character, Tippett rushed to get the goo tube fitted into the puppet when producer [[Gary Kurtz]] questioned the grotesque effect. Nevertheless, director [[George Lucas]] approved the blood-like drool but first filmed the scene without it. On another take, Lucas called for the goo, and Tippett's assistant, [[Laine Liska]], worked the mechanism to release it. The slime shot forth more forcefully and spread farther than intended. Lucas ultimately decided against using the effect in the film due to its messiness.<ref name="TMOSW" /> The character was also referred to as "Snake Head" during shooting, and was later officially dubbed "Nake."<ref name="CRC">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref>

Nevertheless, in [[1995]], [[Judith Reeves-Stevens|Judith]] and [[Garfield Reeves-Stevens]] established the species' name as "Florn Lamproid" and the cantina character as Dice Ibegon in the short story "[[One Last Night in the Mos Eisley Cantina: The Tale of the Wolfman and the Lamproid]]," part of the anthology ''[[Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina]]''.<ref name="CRC" /> "[[Fair Prey]]," a short story published in the ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine's [[Star Wars Gamer|first issue]]<ref name="FP">{{GamerCite|1|Fair Prey}}</ref> in [[November]] [[2000]],<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars Gamer Special Edition]]''</ref> does not capitalize the word "lamproid."<ref name="FP" />

===Non-canon material===
In the [[October 10]], [[2001]]<ref name="Lolli date">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/53987/star_wars_tales_1999_9|text=Star Wars Tales (1999) #9}}</ref> non-[[canon]]ical [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] story "[[Hate Leads to Lollipops]]," published in ''[[Star Wars Tales]]''{{'}} [[Star Wars Tales 9|ninth issue]], a Lamproid with a bib is seated at a [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] [[RIB hutt]] [[Restaurant/Legends|restaurant]].<ref name="Lolli">{{Tales|9|Hate Leads to Lollipops}}</ref> Similarly, a Lamproid makes a cameo in the introduction to [[Star Wars Tales 23|''Star Wars Tales'' 23]] as a spectator at a [[Pazaak/Legends|pazaak]] match played by [[Dark Horse Comics]] editor [[Jeremy Barlow]].<ref name="T23">[[Star Wars Tales 23|''Star Wars Tales'' 23]]</ref> ''Tales'' 23 was published on [[May 11]], [[2005]].<ref name="marv">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/54696/star_wars_tales_1999_23|text=Star Wars Tales (1999) #23}}</ref>
